title: Causal Chain: From Capability Threshold to Deployed Dangerous Model — Where Do Labs Actually Pause?

original_idea.body:
# Causal Chain: From Capability Threshold to Deployed Dangerous Model — Where Do Labs Actually Pause?

**Problem:** Governance frameworks specify that labs should pause or restrict deployment at capability thresholds, but the operational mechanisms by which capability evaluations actually halt or modify deployment are opaque.

**Direction:** Interview-based study (or public document analysis) mapping the decision chain from: capability evaluation result → internal risk assessment → leadership decision → deployment modification. For each publicly documented threshold-adjacent case (Anthropic gray zone, GPT-5.3-Codex High), document what deployment decision was actually made and why.

**Why it matters:** If the causal path from evaluation to deployment decision is broken, capability thresholds are notional governance—they don't actually halt risky deployment. Documenting this chain makes it auditable.

**Relevant context:** Anthropic gray zone Feb 2026 risk report; GPT-5.3-Codex High threshold; Kraprayoon HACCA governance window.
